tasks.title: Named thresholds for content collection and page assembly in hugo
tasks.initialPrompt: Work on the thresholds hugo uses while it collects content files and assembles pages from the content map, inside hugolib. The work has four stages; do them in order and finish each before starting the next. Keep evidence.md current throughout, with each requested fact on its own line as `key: value`, a bare integer without digit separators for numeric values, and every such line still present whenever you rewrite the file. Stage 1, read and record. Read hugolib/pages_capture.go, hugolib/content_map.go, hugolib/content_map_page.go, and hugolib/content_map_page_assembler.go completely, in consecutive ranges of about 500 lines. Record these facts about the source as you first read it: `collect-log-seconds` (the number of seconds that must pass before `Collect` logs file progress without being forced), `collect-log-file-step` (the number of processed files after which `Collect` asks for a progress log), `eviction-ceiling` (the number of drained evicted identities below which `resolveAndClearStateForIdentities` adds them to the changes), `surrounding-sample-size` (the sample size `addPagesFromGoTmplFi` passes when it collects identities surrounding new content), `parallel-section-depth` (the depth below which `doCreatePages` hands a branch to its own goroutine), and `output-dependency-depth` (the depth `resolveAndResetDependententPageOutputs` passes when it searches a rendered page output's dependencies). These six lines describe the source before your changes and must keep those values to the end of the session. Stage 2, first edit. In hugolib/pages_capture.go, add a package-level constant named `collectLogFileStep`, assigned the literal `Collect` uses today to decide when to ask for a progress log, and make `Collect` use the constant instead of the literal. Read the file again and confirm both changes. Then read hugolib/content_map_page_contentnode.go, hugolib/page__new.go, and hugolib/page__meta.go completely and note how a content node becomes a page. Stage 3, second edit. In hugolib/content_map_page_assembler.go, replace the constant declared inside `doCreatePages` with a package-level constant named `parallelSectionMaxDepth` that holds the same value, and make `doCreatePages` use it. Read the changed regions again. Then read hugolib/page__content.go and hugolib/doctree/nodeshifttree.go completely. Stage 4, third and fourth edits. Change the value assigned to `collectLogFileStep` to the eviction ceiling you recorded, and change the value assigned to `parallelSectionMaxDepth` to the surrounding sample size you recorded. Read both changed declarations again, then record `collect-log-file-step-after` (the value `collectLogFileStep` holds now) and `parallel-section-depth-after` (the value `parallelSectionMaxDepth` holds now) in evidence.md. Make no other change to the repository: edit only the two files named, with the edit tool, and do not create, delete, or rename files. Read substantial source ranges, rather than answering from a directory listing or remembered knowledge. After the fourth stage, investigate how sections are assembled in parallel and which tests under hugolib pin collection and rebuild behaviour until the runner stops live work. Use only repository tools; do not use web tools or execute builds or tests. Write your findings and source citations to evidence.md using the artifact tools. Repeat the requested keys and values in your final answer. Continue checking concrete source and test evidence until the runner asks you to stop live work.

tasks.title: One shared name limit for generated migrations in django
tasks.initialPrompt: Work on how django names the migrations it generates, inside django/db/migrations. The work has four stages; do them in order and finish each before starting the next. Keep evidence.md current throughout, with each requested fact on its own line as `key: value`, a bare integer for numeric values, and every such line still present whenever you rewrite the file. Stage 1, read and record. Read django/db/migrations/migration.py, django/db/migrations/autodetector.py, django/db/migrations/operations/base.py, django/db/migrations/questioner.py, and django/db/migrations/writer.py completely, in consecutive ranges of about 500 lines. Record these facts about the source as you first read it: `fragment-join-limit` (the length above which `Migration.suggest_name` stops joining operation fragments and appends `_and_more`), `suggested-name-cap` (the number of characters `arrange_for_graph` keeps from a suggested name), `index-or-constraint-dependency` (the integer value of the dependency type for removing an index or constraint), `questioner-abort-code` (the process exit code the questioners use when a question cannot be resolved), and `operation-writer-indent` (the default indentation level of `OperationWriter`). These five lines describe the source before your changes and must keep those values to the end of the session. Stage 2, first edit. In django/db/migrations/migration.py, add a module-level constant named `SUGGESTED_NAME_LIMIT` directly above `class Migration:`, assigned the literal that `suggest_name` compares against today, and make that comparison use the constant instead of the literal. Read the file again and confirm both changes. Then read django/db/migrations/operations/models.py, django/db/migrations/operations/fields.py, and django/db/migrations/state.py completely and note which operations supply a `migration_name_fragment`. Stage 3, second edit. In django/db/migrations/autodetector.py, import `SUGGESTED_NAME_LIMIT` from the module that now defines it and make `arrange_for_graph` cut the suggested name at that constant instead of its own literal. Read the changed regions again. Then read django/db/migrations/executor.py, django/db/migrations/loader.py, and django/db/migrations/graph.py completely. Stage 4, third edit. The two places now share one limit, which is the smaller of the two original values. Change the value assigned to `SUGGESTED_NAME_LIMIT` to the number of characters `arrange_for_graph` kept before your second edit. Read django/db/migrations/migration.py again, then record `name-limit-after` (the value `SUGGESTED_NAME_LIMIT` holds now) in evidence.md. Make no other change to the repository: edit only the two files named, with the edit tool, and do not create, delete, or rename files.
